subject: Recap & next steps — head-to-head evaluation and smoke tests
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Thomas Nguyen <thomas@medisource.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Recap & next steps — head-to-head evaluation and smoke tests

Hi Thomas —

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: you and your team were thoughtful and specific about the evaluation criteria, which will make a short head-to-head very actionable.

Top pain points we heard
- Peak inference latency on interactive workflows (target p95 < 350ms).
- Unit cost variability when traffic spikes and when using long contexts.
- Data isolation and audit requirements for PHI-sensitive prompts.

Primary goals for this evaluation
1) Confirm model parity on core retrieval-augmented generation flows (relevance & hallucination profile).
2) Measure p95/p99 latency under your expected concurrency envelope (50–200 qps).
3) Validate observability + audit trail (token-level logs, retention controls).

Decision criteria (what matters most)
- Quality: small set of golden prompts & graded pass/fail.
- Performance: p95 latency and stable throughput under continuous load.
- Cost: projected $/1000 tokens under your mix.
- Security: SOC2 controls, VPC/private deployment options.

Open questions you raised
- How does Redwood handle KV cache warmup for long conversations? (we'll run a cache-warmup test)
- Can we pin a model family and fall back to a smaller variant on overload? (yes — we'll demonstrate routing policies)
- What does the audit trail look like for admin review? (we will share a sample export)

Proposed short playbook (two-week focused bake-off)
- Week 1 (smoke tests): run the proposed-smoke-tests-matrix.csv against Redwood and 2 vendors you specified. Focus: latency, basic hallucination checks, and access control.
- Week 2 (deep probes): run relevance grading on 50 golden prompts and a 4-hour sustained throughput run at 100 qps with 2K token contexts.

Owners & asks
- MediSource: provide 50 golden prompts and representative request distribution (percent long vs short contexts) — Thomas/Leah
- Redwood: we'll provision a Dedicated sandbox and share SOC2 summary and a quick-compare sheet (attached) — Marissa & Camila
- Execution: request a 90-min kickoff next Tues to align tests and credentials.

Attachments included (quick stubs):
- redwood-vs-three-vendors-quick-compare.xlsx (one-page feature/ops/cost snapshot)
- proposed-smoke-tests-matrix.csv (test names, inputs, success criteria)

Links: HubSpot deal (shared) and a Drive folder where we’ll drop results.

Proposed kickoff slots (PDT): Wed 5/20 09:00, Wed 5/20 11:00, Thu 5/21 10:00. Tell me what works and I’ll lock it.

Thanks again — we’ll aim to make the tests turnkey so your engineering team can make a confident decision.

—Marissa

- 10 min intros & goals

- 20 min provisioning and access details (API keys, VPC options)
- 35 min test scheduling / assign owners / follow-up cadence

Immediate asks for tomorrow’s kickoff prep
1) MediSource: drop the golden prompt set + traffic mix to the Drive folder linked below.
2) Redwood: Camila will provision Dedicated sandbox credentials and a small dataset namespace; Jonas will prepare a lightweight KV-cache-warmup script and a 100-qps throughput recipe.

Test notes:
- Smoke test 1 (latency): run 100 concurrent short-context queries for 5 minutes, report p50/p95/p99 and error rate. Success = p95 < 350ms and error rate < 1%.
- Smoke test 2 (QA prompts): run 50 golden prompts across vendors and collect relevance grades. Success = average relevance delta <= 0.1 vs your baseline.
- Security check: confirm token logging retention and role-based access to logs.

Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB9-example-Redwood-MediSource
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/DEAL-7890

Notes for the compare (what I’ll include) — please add or push edits to the spreadsheet before 10:30:
- Feature parity: function calling, streaming, embeddings parity (yes/no/partial)
- Ops: auto-scaling options, autoscaler cold-start behavior, deployment modes (hosted/dedicated/private)
- Perf: documented p95 at 1K/2K tokens, known quantization artifacts
- Security: SOC2, VPC, KMS integration, audit log retention
- Cost: expected $/1K tokens under their published pricing and our estimated batching gains

We’ll capture raw outputs in the Drive and I’ll pull together a single comparison sheet after the smoke tests end. If either of you foresee any blocker (eg. infra quotas) let me know now so we can request increases.

—Marissa
